name: אֶשְׁבַּעַל
gloss: man of Baal (of the lord); or Baal is
summary: The name Chronicles gives to Saul’s fourth son (1Ch 8:33; 9:39), whom Samuel calls אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת, Ish-bosheth, the king Abner set over Israel (2Sa 2:8–10). Samuel’s form writes the first part as אִישׁ, “man of”, which is scripture’s own reading of it, and puts בֹּשֶׁת “shame” for בַּעַל. בַּעַל is “owner, lord, husband”, and in Saul’s day could be said of Yahweh, as Hos 2:18 shows by ending the practice: “you shall call me my man (אִישִׁי), and shall no longer call me my Baal (בַּעְלִי)”. The pointing אֶשְׁ־ is not that of אִישׁ, and a Punic name ʾšbʿl is read “Baal is (alive)”, with ʾš the word “there is” (Hebrew יֵשׁ, אִשׁ); that reading cannot be ruled out, so both are given.

evidence.note: “Saul begot Jonathan and Malchi-shua and Abinadab and אֶשְׁבָּעַל.”
The same son of Saul written אִישׁ בֹּשֶׁת: the first part read as אִישׁ, the second replaced.
אִישִׁי and בַּעְלִי side by side as names by which Israel called Yahweh, the second to be used no more.
“I will take the names of the Baals out of her mouth.”
Another name with בַּעַל in Saul’s house: Jonathan’s son מְרִיב בַּעַל.
אִשׁ for יֵשׁ, “is there?”: the word the second reading takes the first part to be; also 2Sa 14:19.

evidence.locator: p. 81, ʾŠBʿL = YŠBʿL, p.n. (“Baal is alive”); “Compare Heb. ʾešbaʿal (1 Chronicles 8:33); Ug. iṯbʿl”
evidence.note: The Punic name, read with ʾš “there is”.
Phoenician ʾš “man”, written without y as in אֶשְׁ־.

note: Both tokens of a.gb.ai are this name (1Ch 8:33; 9:39), pausal אֶשְׁבָּעַל. Filed with אִישׁ because Samuel’s parallel form spells the first part אִישׁ; if the reviewer prefers “Baal is” (אִשׁ / יֵשׁ, Ugaritic iṯ), the name belongs with יֵשׁ instead and cognate_ids should be dropped. A third reading, “fire of Baal” (אֵשׁ), has no support in the parallel form and is not given. The same person as names/ish-bosheth, so both name entries tag Ish-bosheth@2Sa.2.8.
